results.title: “Retire Statistical Significance”: The discussion.
results.content: *   ![Image 2](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/087d4b749e60debf59b5e01898364a91?s=39&d=identicon&r=g)Christian Hennig on [March 25, 2019 12:01 PM at 12:01 pm](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2019/03/20/retire-statistical-significance-the-discussion/#comment-1001984)said: Like often I’m coming too late to this discussion, but the first thing that strikes me is that the first two postings state that the article that is discussed asks for abandoning p-values, which it quite explicitly doesn’t. *   ![Image 24](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/1e06a63a135ea67cf41a9f45c54de7ad?s=39&d=identicon&r=g)Anoneuoid on [March 20, 2019 7:49 PM at 7:49 pm](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2019/03/20/retire-statistical-significance-the-discussion/#comment-998135)said: Also, isn’t it strange that almost all (except ~5) the SNPs that met p < 5e-8 for the current study (all must have in the original to be included here) are above the diagonal and it looks like only one with a “lesser” p-values is above? *   ![Image 26](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/1e06a63a135ea67cf41a9f45c54de7ad?s=39&d=identicon&r=g)Anoneuoid on [March 21, 2019 7:57 AM at 7:57 am](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2019/03/20/retire-statistical-significance-the-discussion/#comment-998595)said: > What they are saying here is that if in the previous study, they found a positive effect for “AGTC” at one locus over other possible alleles, they then also plotted the effect size for “AGTC” in the replication cohort (and not some other allele like “AGTA” or “AGTT”).
